trait_coordinate: floral display and reproductive effort across edge-gap context
eligibility_reason: Edges and gaps alter flower production, fruit set and robbery rate, but the source does not estimate two functional responses to one declared plant trait coordinate.
source_basis: Magrach et al. 2012 Austral Ecology DOI 10.1111/j.1442-9993.2011.02320.x
notes: Nectar robbing is much higher in gappy patches and lowers reproductive success; this is ecological-context dependence rather than same-axis conflict.

eligibility_reason: Avian pollinators spend more time on white morphs, but that behavioral difference has no apparent fecundity consequence and surviving seed production is not directly associated with color.
notes: Color is a pollinator-facing signal but the source does not support a matched negative seed-predator selection component on color.

eligibility_reason: Flower number is positively associated with nectar production, seed-predator occurrence and total long-term seed production, but seeds surviving predation are not directly associated with flower number.
notes: The dominant fecundity path is not an identified opposing pollinator-versus-seed-predator geometry.

trait_coordinate: flowering schedule and congener floral syndrome
antagonist_guild: moth/fly flower predators and weevil seed predator
eligibility_reason: Sequentially flowering congeners differ simultaneously in phenology, floral morphology and breeding system, so species differences cannot be promoted to one trait-axis geometry.
notes: The early species is pollen limited but does not consistently escape flower/seed predation; the study is an ecological comparison, not a same-axis conflict test.

eligibility_reason: Flower size, herkogamy and mating system covary geographically; florivory is higher in large-flowered populations but large-flowered individuals are not generally more vulnerable within populations.
source_basis: Dart et al. programme; Annals of Botany 2015 PMCID PMC4551092 plus Queen's dissertation source
notes: Reduced floral parasitism in small-flowered selfing populations is interpreted as an ecological consequence rather than a demonstrated driver of the mating-system transition.

eligibility_reason: Chemotype affects florivore visits and marginally pollinator visits in one plot context; germination varies with chemotype and pollinator visitation but not florivore visitation.
source_basis: Sasidharan et al. 2024 Functional Ecology DOI 10.1111/1365-2435.14673; preprint SCHPRISMA-000352
notes: Individual chemical identity does not resolve as a stable pollinator-florivore conflict; realized effects depend on visitor group and plot context.

eligibility_reason: Heterogeneous plots receive more pollinator visits, while plot type has no significant effect on florivore visits or germination success.
source_basis: Sasidharan et al. 2024 Functional Ecology DOI 10.1111/1365-2435.14673; preprint SCHPRISMA-000352
notes: A clean one-sided visitor response at the neighborhood chemical-diversity scale.

antagonist_guild: Trigona spinipes and other floral antagonists
eligibility_reason: Many-flowered individuals are more central and receive more visits; antagonists dominate the network and reduce reproductive success, but this source does not re-estimate trait-specific opposing selection on flower number.
notes: Same biological flower-number axis as SCHPRISMA-000312; use as additional network context, not an independent canonical trait axis.

antagonist_guild: Trigona spinipes and other floral antagonists
eligibility_reason: Centrality is an emergent network property rather than a declared plant phenotypic coordinate, so it does not enter H1 trait-axis models.
